members.reason: Describes the goal of the same convening (a culture of discussion and shared agreements among stakeholders) — interchangeable facet of the periodic stakeholder forum proposal.
Proposes convening stakeholders representing the range of views into a periodically-meeting forum for discussion and agreement — the same specific intervention.
Calls for significant motivation, patience and persistence through the long change process — same dispositional lever.
'Stubbornness' — maintain consistency and commitment through the research process despite difficulties — interchangeable with the persistence/perseverance statement.
Committed, academically professional team implementing on the basis of academic knowledge — matches the committed-leading-actor-bridging-academia-and-field core.
A committed leading actor invested in both academic knowledge and field implementation — this IS the core proposal.
A general goal of making research practical and implementable — no leading-actor lever; a goal statement, not the same intervention.
Strengthening applied research is a different lever (change the kind of research) than appointing a committed leading implementer.
'Successful collaboration' is a vague sentiment fragment with no specific action — not interchangeable with appointing a leading actor.
'Combining knowledge and involvement for environmental change' is a vague slogan with a different focus, not the leading-actor intervention.
Avoiding the ivory tower by including users' voices in the research process is a different intervention (participatory research), not appointing an implementation leader.
Researchers working with end users affected by the research is the participatory-research proposal, not the committed-leading-actor proposal.
Personal acquaintance with a person who researched and understands the topic — same enabling factor as the other member.
Personal acquaintance as the key, via conferences emphasizing unmediated human connection — same factor, only adds the venue as illustration.
Simplifying research problems into accessible, non-threatening, clear discourse for different sectors — the audience-adapted-language lever.
Knowing how to speak the target audience's language — same intervention, terser formulation.
Incentives and supports for executing the change target the change-implementers, a different lever and target than funding the research itself (the core shared by Jf82/BH5P).
'Related to economic benefit' is a fragment/sentiment with no proposed action — not interchangeable with a resource-allocation proposal.
Allocate required resources (budgets, materials, tech tools) to support research initiatives — the fund-the-research core.
Allocate financial resources for conducting the research (equipment, staff, expenses) — interchangeable with Jf82's resource allocation.
A connecting agent who extracts the data clearly and makes the interpersonal connection that changes reality — the core proposal.
Near-verbatim restatement: interpersonal relationships as the bridge letting the researcher present data clearly and create the connection that drives change.
'Vacuum of information' is a pure problem statement with no intervention — merging a problem with the webinar solution violates the rubric.
Regular webinars to make the most relevant knowledge accessible — the concrete core proposal.
Understanding the place — its information layers and needs — as the basis for changing reality; same ground-the-research-in-field-understanding lever, terse formulation.
Research question derived from observation and deep understanding of the field need — the core proposal.
Preliminary fieldwork that prepares the ground and sharpens the project — same intervention: invest in field understanding before/for the research.
'The power of field research: surfacing challenges and developing solutions' is a general value claim about field-based research, not the specific derive-questions-from-field-understanding action.
Involve the public in strategic processes and decisions so it can influence research direction and implementation — the core proposal.
'Research can drive big things' is a generic sentiment about research's power, saying nothing about public involvement — a different topic entirely.
Connecting academia, civil society and government to promote collaboration and innovation — the cross-sector partnership core.
'Matchmaking' between researchers, civil-society organizations and government ministries — the same intervention stated concretely.
Building collaborations between academia, industry and social organizations to drive research projects — same cross-sector-partnership lever; the partner list varies but the intervention does not.
Forming partnerships with academic institutions, social organizations or businesses as a lever for change — interchangeable with the other partnership members.
